title: Stop the carton
objective: Keep the conveyor off at idle. A one-scan Process Start request must keep it moving after Start releases. Stop at the photoeye and hold position. A one-scan Process Stop must stop and hold. Simultaneous Start and Stop must stay off. Start while the beam is occupied must stay off. Reset Attempt keeps your ladder and reloads the carton; a fresh Start must repeat the behavior. Process Stop is an ordinary simulated input, not a certified protective function.
hints: Run Simulation and use Process Start once. Observe the conveyor command after Start releases. A momentary request is not a maintained input.
Consider how your BOOL logic can remember a run request between scans. A normal Assign coil updates its target each scan; an output or an unbound memory BOOL can be read by contacts.

Find every condition that must inhibit the conveyor command: Process Stop and occupied photoeye. Those conditions must dominate a Start request and the remembered request. Reset Attempt clears runtime state but keeps your ladder.

glossary.meaning: One accepted scan of true requests motion. The button is momentary; releasing it does not provide memory.
Ordinary simulated process input, true for one accepted scan. It must dominate Start. It is separate from Stop Simulation and provides no certified safety function.
True when the carton blocks the modeled beam. Feedback comes from actual model travel; the learner must not write this input.
True commands modeled motion. It is a command, not independent motor feedback. Coordinates are symbolic; this model does not establish wiring, physical safety or commissioning readiness.
